newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Katyusha rocket hits Israel, warplanes retaliate.
newsitem.headline: Katyusha rocket hits Israel, warplanes retaliate.

text.p: A Katyusha rocket fired from south Lebanon slammed into Israel on Wednesday, raising the tension along the Jewish state's northern border but causing no injuries, the Israeli army said.
Israel warplanes retaliated swiftly, twice raiding suspected targets of Islamic guerrillas in south Lebanon, Lebanese security sources said.
The planes fired five rockets into Iqlim al-Toufah ridge, controlled by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas, the Lebanese sources said.
"According to initial reports it appears one Katyusha was fired at western Galilee. At this stage we know of no injuries or damage," said an Israeli army spokesman.

The Katyusha attack was only the second in nine months since a ceasefire agreement in April 1996 banned pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas from firing Katyushas into northern Israel. The U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding ended a 17-day Israeli blitz against pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon.

Pro-Israeli militia sources in Lebanon had said several Katyusha rockets fired from north of the Israeli-held zone slammed into the Western Galilee and the border strip near the Lebanon-Israel frontier.
No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.
A Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman in Beirut declined to comment on the rocket attack. "We have no information on this matter," he told Reuters.
The air raids were the latest strike in a tit-for-tat war between Israel and Hizbollah (Party of God) militants fighting to oust the Jewish state from its south Lebanon occupation zone.
Pro-Israeli militia sources in Lebanon said Hizbollah guerrillas killed one Israeli soldier and wounded four in a clash on Wednesday in the 15-km (nine mile) wide occupation zone.

"It was a close-range clash between the guerrillas and the Israelis. The guerrillas used machineguns and anti-tank rockets. Five Israelis were wounded and one of them died later," a source from Israel's 3,000-strong South Lebanon Army (SLA) client militia in the border zone said. Hizbollah claimed responsibility for the attack.
Earlier in the day a mine exploded in south Lebanon, wounding three Israeli soldiers, security sources said.
Around 1,000 Israeli troops patrol the zone that the Jewish state carved out in 1985 to prevent cross-border raids.
